title: Sectionwise invariance of Hom complexes into K-injectives with independent coefficient universe
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $s:I^{\prime\bullet}\to I^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $t:L^{\prime\bullet}\to L^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For every site object $U$, the section map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I^{\prime})\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L^{\prime},I))$ induced by precomposition with $t$ and postcomposition with $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism of abelian-group complexes. Here the Hom complexes are those of [def-pur-hom-complex]. This universe-general form takes C : Type u with Category v and coefficient/module universe max u v r, for arbitrary r; assume abelian-group sheafification and its locally bijective characterization on the original site. It uses the same sheaves, restriction, Hom complex, differentials, and induced maps as the original source statement.

proof.text: Work with objects in Type u, arrows in Type v, and coefficient rings and modules in Type (max u v r). Use the existing siteAbelianHasSheafify and siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective instances on the slice whenever an abelian or exactness instance is needed. All these instances are proved, and the given base-site instances are retained.

Install the zero-morphism compatibility of restriction from module_overFunctor_preservesZero. For each n, invoke the shifted local derived comparison with its pre/postcomposition naturality. Obtain equivalences a and b between section homology and the localized derived Hom sets.

Restrict both s and t using localizedModule_restriction_quasiIso. Their derived images, including the shift of s, are isomorphisms. The function h↦Q(t)≫h≫Q(s[n]) is bijective: composition with inv Q(t) and inv Q(s[n]) is its inverse.

Naturality identifies b composed with the section homology map with this bijection composed with a. Cancel the bijection b to obtain bijectivity of the homology map, convert to IsIso in AddCommGrpCat, and assemble QuasiIsoAt for every n into QuasiIso.
